'''Vasily Astratov''' is a full professor of Physics and Optical Science at the [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte]]. He became known for launching [[Synthetic opal#Synthetic opal|synthetic opals]] as new self-assembled [[photonic crystal]]s for visible light in 1995 in his former group at [[Ioffe Institute]] in Russia (jointly with [[Yurii Vlasov]], Alexander Kaplyanskii and co-authors).<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Astratov | first1=V. N. | last2=Bogomolov | first2=V. N. | last3=Kaplyanskii | first3=A. A. | last4=Prokofiev | first4=A. V. | last5=Samoilovich | first5=L. A. | last6=Samoilovich | first6=S. M. | last7=Vlasov | first7=Yu. A. | title=Optical spectroscopy of opal matrices with CdS embedded in its pores: Quantum confinement and photonic band gap effects | journal=Il Nuovo Cimento D | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=17 | issue=11–12 | year=1995 | issn=0392-6737 | doi=10.1007/bf02457208 | pages=1349–1354| bibcode=1995NCimD..17.1349A | s2cid=121167426 }}</ref> This work has resulted in a quest for inverse opals with a complete three-dimensional [[photonic band gap]].

==Early life==
He received his M.S. from the [[Saint Petersburg State University]], Russia, in 1981, and received his Ph.D. degree from the [[Ioffe Institute|A.F. Ioffe Physical-Technical Institute]], St. Petersburg, in 1986. At this institution he had accomplished a career as a research scientist, rising through the ranks from staff member (1981–1992), group leader (1992–1997), to senior member of staff in 1997. In 1997–2001 he worked as a postdoctoral scholar at the [[University of Sheffield]] where he developed novel surface coupling techniques for studying photonic crystal waveguides and semiconductor microcavities.

==Research==
Prof. V. N. Astratov joined [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte|UNC-Charlotte]] in 2002. His current research is devoted to microspherical [[photonics]] including applications of photonic nanojets, coupled-cavity arrays<ref>V.N. Astratov, [https://web.archive.org/web/20140728035214/http://clas-pages.uncc.edu/vasily-astratov/files/2012/11/Chapter-17-Astratov.pdf Photonic Microresonator Research and Applications, Ch. 17, pp. 423–457, Springer, New York (2010)]</ref> and waveguides<ref name=":0">{{cite journal | last1=Astratov | first1=V. N. | last2=Franchak | first2=J. P. | last3=Ashili | first3=S. P. | title=Optical coupling and transport phenomena in chains of spherical dielectric microresonators with size disorder | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=85 | issue=23 | date=2004-12-06 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.1832737 | pages=5508–5510| bibcode=2004ApPhL..85.5508A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Allen | first1=Kenneth W. | last2=Darafsheh | first2=Arash | last3=Abolmaali | first3=Farzaneh | last4=Mojaverian | first4=Neda | last5=Limberopoulos | first5=Nicholaos I. | last6=Lupu | first6=Anatole | last7=Astratov | first7=Vasily N. | title=Microsphere-chain waveguides: Focusing and transport properties | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=105 | issue=2 | date=2014-07-14 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.4890595 | page=021112| bibcode=2014ApPhL.105b1112A | doi-access=free }}</ref> resonant [[Radiation pressure|light pressure]] effects<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Li | first1=Yangcheng | ''Optics Express''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://proxy.osapublishing.org/oe/home.cfm|title=OSA &#124; Optics Express|website=proxy.osapublishing.org}}</ref> in 2005–2011 and an editor and co-editor for two Focus Issues of this journal. He has served as a technical committee member for major international conferences including CLEO<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cleoconference.org/home/|title=Home &#124; CLEO}}</ref> 2006–07 and 2012–14, IEEE Photonics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ieee-ipc.org/|title=IEEE Photonics Conference – Annual Meeting of the IEEE Photonics Society|website=ieee-ipc.org}}</ref> 2014–17, Photonics West 2017, ICTON 2009–17, and [[OECC]]/ACOFT 2008 and 2014. He co-/authored 15 patents in the US and Russia, and about 180 research publications which eventually brought him an h-index of 44.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=I9fTI70AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Vasily Astratov|publisher=[[Google Scholar]]|access-date=May 16, 2014}}</ref>

==Awards==
He is a recipient of a number of awards including International Visitor Award in France by Triangle de la Physique in 2011, Senior Visiting [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] Fellow Award in the UK in 2006, Award of the Exchange Program adopted between [[Royal Society]] and [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1996, and the Award in the Annual Competition from [[Ioffe Institute|A.F. Ioffe Physical-Technical Institute]] in 1985.
